plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, since your payment (second-highest bid) doesn't depend on your own bid unless you're the winner, and overbidding/underbidding only risks winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my value of $24, ignoring speculation about opponents' beliefs since truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid or believe, since your payment doesn't depend on your own bid (only on whether you win). Overthinking about others' beliefs doesn't change this: truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $16, so I will bid exactly that.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, truthful bidding (bidding exactly your value) is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since your bid only affects whether you win, not what you pay if you win. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
